questions.question: Find the LCM of (2)/(5), (3)/(5) and (1)/(2).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

LCM of fractions = LCM(Numerators) ÷ HCF(Denominators)

Numerators: 2, 3, 1 → LCM = 6

Denominators: 5, 5, 2 → HCF = 1

Required LCM = 6 ÷ 1 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given Fractions: 2/5, 3/5, 1/2

Formula used: LCM of Fractions = LCM(Numerators) ÷ HCF(Denominators)

 
 LCM of Numerators (2, 3, 1) = 6
 
• 
 
 HCF of Denominators (5, 5, 2) = 1

⇒ Identify the numerators: 2, 3, and 1.

⇒ Multiples of 2: 2, 4, 6, 8, ...

⇒ Multiples of 3: 3, 6, 9, ...

⇒ Multiples of 1: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, ...

⇒ Least Common Multiple (LCM) of (2, 3, 1) = 6

⇒ Identify the denominators: 5, 5, and 2.

⇒ Factors of 5: 1, 5

⇒ Factors of 2: 1, 2

⇒ Highest Common Factor (HCF) of (5, 5, 2) = 1

⇒ LCM of Fractions = 6 ÷ 1 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF of Fractions

To find the Highest Common Factor of fractions, use the formula: HCF of Fractions = HCF(Numerators) ÷ LCM(Denominators).

Simplest Form Requirement

Before applying LCM/HCF formulas, always ensure all given fractions are reduced to their lowest (simplest) terms.

Relationship for Two Numbers

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).</p

questions.question: Find the sum of the numbers between 550 and 700 such that when they are divided by 12, 16 and 24, leave remainder 5 in each case.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Common divisor = **LCM**(12, 16, 24) = 48.

Numbers are of form **48k + 5**.

For range 550 − 700: k = 12 (581), k = 13 (629), k = 14 (677).

Sum = 581 + 629 + 677 = 1887.

**∴ The correct answer is 1887.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1f48bbb2c97ef02b5356cad106ae7e88b282cddeecef97cd6a3e9d9f462ea573.png] 

**Given:** Divisors are 12, 16, and 24. Remainder in each case is 5. Range is 550 to 700.

**Formula:** Number = **LCM(divisors) × k + remainder**

⇒ LCM(12, 16, 24):

⇒ 12 = 2² × 3, 16 = 2⁴, 24 = 2³ × 3

⇒ LCM = 2⁴ × 3 = 16 × 3 = 48

⇒ General form = 48k + 5

⇒ If k = 12, Number = 48 × 12 + 5 = 576 + 5 = 581

⇒ If k = 13, Number = 48 × 13 + 5 = 624 + 5 = 629

⇒ If k = 14, Number = 48 × 14 + 5 = 672 + 5 = 677

⇒ If k = 15, Number = 48 × 15 + 5 = 720 + 5 = 725 (Outside range)

⇒ Sum = 581 + 629 + 677 = 1887

**∴ The correct answer is 1887.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Method for Remainders

When a number leaves the same remainder 'r' when divided by x, y, and z, the number is of the form **LCM(x, y, z)k + r**.

Arithmetic Progression Sum

If the found numbers form an AP, the sum can also be calculated as **n/2 × (first term + last term)**.

Different Remainders

If remainders are different such that (divisor − remainder) = constant (d), then the number is **LCM(divisors)k − d**.</p

questions.question: John got 20% marks in an examination and failed by 10 marks. In the same examination, Jack got 35% marks which were 20 more than the minimum passing marks. Find the percentage of minimum marks required to pass.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in Percentage = 35% − 20% = 15%

Difference in Marks = 20 − (−10) = 30 marks

15% → 30 marks ∴ 1% → 2 marks

John needs 10 more marks to pass → 10 ÷ 2 = 5% extra

Passing Percentage = 20% + 5% = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

John: 20% marks, Failed by 10 marks.

Jack: 35% marks, 20 marks more than pass.

**Formula Used:**

Passing Marks = (Total Marks × Pass %) / 100

 
• 
 
 
 20% (John)
 
 
 Pass %
 
 
 35% (Jack)
 
 

 +10 marks
 
 

 −20 marks
 
 Total Gap = 30 Marks = 15%

Let the total marks be x.

⇒ Passing marks = (20/100) × x + 10

⇒ Passing marks = (35/100) × x − 20

⇒ 0.20x + 10 = 0.35x − 20

⇒ 10 + 20 = 0.35x − 0.20x

⇒ 30 = 0.15x

⇒ x = 30 / 0.15

⇒ x = 200 marks

⇒ Passing marks = (20/100) × 200 + 10 = 40 + 10 = 50 marks

⇒ Passing percentage = (50 / 200) × 100

⇒ Passing percentage = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

To find the percentage change, use the formula: % Change = (Difference / Original Value) × 100.

Total Marks Calculation

Total Marks = (Sum of marks deficiency and excess) / (Difference in percentage) × 100.

Passing Marks Relation

Passing Marks = Passed Marks − Excess Marks OR Failed Marks + Marks Deficiency.</p

questions.question: The radius of a right circular cylinder is 21 cm and its curved surface area is 5280 cm². What is its volume?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Relationship between **Volume (V)**, **Curved Surface Area (CSA)**, and **Radius (r)** of a cylinder:

**Volume** = (CSA × r) ÷ 2

⇒ Volume = (5280 × 21) ÷ 2

⇒ Volume = 2640 × 21 = 55440 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 55440 cm³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Radius (r)** = 21 cm

⇒ **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 5280 cm²

**Formula Used:**

⇒ CSA of cylinder = 2 × π × r × h

⇒ Volume of cylinder = π × r² × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67aa640f7601eb29dae1cfcc48d19169e16de43fa7110102288a104eb5080fea.png] 

**Step 1: Calculate Height (h)**

⇒ 5280 = 2 × (22/7) × 21 × h

⇒ 5280 = 2 × 22 × 3 × h

⇒ 5280 = 132 × h

⇒ h = 5280 ÷ 132 = 40 cm

**Step 2: Calculate Volume (V)**

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 21 × 21 × 40

⇒ Volume = 22 × 3 × 21 × 40

⇒ Volume = 66 × 840

⇒ Volume = 55440 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 55440 cm³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cylinder

The TSA includes the **curved surface** and the **two circular bases**: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

Volume Comparison with Cone

For the same **radius** and **height**, the **Volume of a Cone** is exactly 1/3rd the **Volume of a Cylinder** (V = 1/3 × πr²h).

Area of Base

The base of a cylinder is a **circle**, so its area is πr². Volume can also be written as **Base Area × Height**.</p

questions.question: A boat takes 28 hours for travelling downstream from point A to point B and coming back to point C midway between A and B. If the velocity of the stream is 6 km/h, and the speed of the boat in still water is 9 km/h, what is the distance between A and B?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Downstream Speed** = 9 + 6 = 15 km/h; **Upstream Speed** = 9 − 6 = 3 km/h.

Let total distance **AB** = x km. Then distance **BC** = x/2 km.

Total time = Time(**A→B**) + Time(**B→C**) = x/15 + (x/2)/3 = 28 hours.

x/15 + x/6 = 28 ⇒ (2x + 5x)/30 = 28 ⇒ 7x/30 = 28.

x = (28 × 30) ÷ 7 = 120 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 km.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of boat in **Still Water** (u) = 9 km/h

Speed of **Stream** (v) = 6 km/h

Total time taken for the trip = 28 hours

**Formula Used:**

**Downstream Speed** (Sd) = u + v

**Upstream Speed** (Sᵤ) = u − v

**Time** = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/84a67fb8665afb3d4102475ea7ba727b226bb749cb981d12a67b7d3964d5791f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Downstream Speed** = 9 + 6 = 15 km/h

⇒ **Upstream Speed** = 9 − 6 = 3 km/h

⇒ Let distance **AB** = D km. Since **C** is the **midway** point, **BC** = D/2 km.

⇒ Time for **A to B** (Downstream) = D/15 hours

⇒ Time for **B to C** (Upstream) = (D/2) ÷ 3 = D/6 hours

⇒ Total Time = D/15 + D/6 = 28

⇒ (2D + 5D) ÷ 30 = 28

⇒ 7D/30 = 28

⇒ D = (28 × 30) ÷ 7

⇒ D = 4 × 30 = 120 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 km.**

**__Additional Information__**

Downstream and Upstream Basics

The speed of a boat in the direction of the stream is Sd = u + v, and against the stream is Sᵤ = u − v, where u is speed in **Still Water** and v is **Stream Velocity**.

Speed in Still Water from Sd and Sᵤ

The speed of the boat in **Still Water** can be calculated as u = (Sd + Sᵤ) ÷ 2.

Stream Velocity from Sd and Sᵤ

The velocity of the **Stream** can be calculated as v = (Sd − Sᵤ) ÷ 2.</p

questions.question: ∆XYZ and ∆PQR are similar. XY ∶ PQ = 6 ∶ 1. Area of ∆PQR is 6 cm². What is the area of ∆XYZ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **corresponding sides** of similar triangles ΔXYZ and ΔPQR is 6 ÷ 1.

Ratio of their **areas** = (Ratio of sides)² = (6)² ÷ (1)² = 36 ÷ 1.

Given, Area of ΔPQR = 6 cm².

Area of ΔXYZ = 36 × Area of ΔPQR = 36 × 6 = 216 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 216 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ΔXYZ ∼ ΔPQR

Ratio of sides XY ÷ PQ = 6 ÷ 1

Area of ΔPQR = 6 cm²

**Formula Used:**

For two **similar triangles**, the ratio of their areas is equal to the **square** of the ratio of their corresponding sides:

Area(ΔXYZ) ÷ Area(ΔPQR) = (XY ÷ PQ)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e40db5bf7be8c27939ea7c972347fe6456a6434217f1f9d0247bf6e6892f12e7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area(ΔXYZ) ÷ 6 = (6 ÷ 1)²

⇒ Area(ΔXYZ) ÷ 6 = 36 ÷ 1

⇒ Area(ΔXYZ) = 36 × 6

⇒ Area(ΔXYZ) = 216

**∴ The correct answer is 216 cm².**

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding altitudes, medians, or angle bisectors.

Perimeter of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides: P₁ ÷ P₂ = s₁ ÷ s₂.

Criteria for Similarity

Two triangles are similar if their corresponding angles are equal (AA) or if their corresponding sides are in the same proportion (SSS/SAS).</p

questions.question: What is the value of, sin 150° × cos 0° × tan 67° × tan 23° × tan 45°
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If the sum of two angles A and B is 90°, then tan A × tan B = 1.

Here, 67° + 23° = 90° ⇒ tan 67° × tan 23° = 1

Also we know the standard values: sin 150° = 1 / 2, cos 0° = 1, and tan 45° = 1.

Result = (1 / 2) × 1 × 1 × 1 = 1 / 2

**∴ The correct answer is 1 / 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = sin 150° × cos 0° × tan 67° × tan 23° × tan 45°

**Formula Used:**

⇒ sin(180° − θ) = sin θ

⇒ tan(90° − θ) = cot θ

⇒ tan θ × cot θ = 1

**Calculation:**

⇒ sin 150° = sin(180° − 30°) = sin 30° = 1 / 2

⇒ cos 0° = 1

⇒ tan 67° = tan(90° − 23°) = cot 23°

⇒ tan 67° × tan 23° = cot 23° × tan 23° = 1

⇒ tan 45° = 1

Substituting all the simplified values back into the expression:

⇒ Expression = (1 / 2) × 1 × 1 × 1

⇒ Expression = 1 / 2

**∴ The correct answer is 1 / 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles in Trigonometry

Two angles are complementary if their sum is 90°. Key transformations: tan(90° − θ) = cot θ | sin(90° − θ) = cos θ | sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.

Supplementary Angles

Two angles are supplementary if their sum is 180°. In the second quadrant, sine is positive: sin(180° − θ) = sin θ. Cosine and tangent are negative: cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ | tan(180° − θ) = −tan θ.

Important Trigonometric Product Rule

Whenever the sum of two angles A and B is 90° (A + B = 90°), the product of their tangents is always 1: tan A × tan B = 1.

questions.question: Divide 1870 into three parts in such a way that half of the first part, one-third of the second part, and one-sixth of the third part are equal. Then, the third part is _______.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The given condition **1/2 of A = 1/3 of B = 1/6 of C** directly gives the **Ratio** of the parts as **A : B : C = 2 : 3 : 6**.

Sum of ratio parts = 2 + 3 + 6 = **11 units**.

Total amount = 1870, so 11 units = 1870 ⇒ 1 unit = **170**.

The **Third part (C)** corresponds to 6 units ⇒ 6 × 170 = **1020**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1020.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total amount = 1870. Let the three parts be **x**, **y**, and **z**.

**Condition:** (1/2)x = (1/3)y = (1/6)z

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca38c7fab472a61a2d8a0b89c98d0058afabfb6ceec9d4b7825b0f5170b5d29d.png] 

Let (1/2)x = (1/3)y = (1/6)z = **k**

⇒ x = 2k, y = 3k, z = 6k

Since the sum of the parts is the **Total amount**:

⇒ x + y + z = 1870

⇒ 2k + 3k + 6k = 1870

⇒ 11k = 1870

⇒ k = 1870 ÷ 11

⇒ k = 170

The **Third part** is z = 6k:

⇒ z = 6 × 170 = 1020

**∴ The correct answer is 1020.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion

Dividing a Quantity into Parts

To divide a number N into the ratio a:b:c, calculate the value of one part as N/(a+b+c) and multiply by the required ratio coefficient.

Equivalent Ratios

Multiplying or dividing all terms of a **ratio** by the same non-zero number does not change the ratio (e.g., 2:3:6 is the same as 4:6:12).</p

questions.question: If the area of rectangle is 168 cm² and the diagonal length is 25 cm, then find the perimeter of the rectangle. (in cm)

Diagonal length = 25 cm

(1.) Area of rectangle = l × b

(2.) Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b)

(3.) Diagonal length = √(l² + b²)

Where, 

l = length of the rectangle

b = breadth of the rectangle

Algebraic identity:

(4.) (x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy

Now,

⇒ lb = 168 ----(2)

Now,

⇒ (l + b)² = l² + b² + 2lb

⇒ (l + b)2 = 625 + 2(168)

⇒ (l + b)2 = 625 + 336

⇒ (l + b)2 = 961

⇒ l + b = 31

⇒ Cancelling the common term (1 − cos A) from numerator and denominator:

⇒ Result = 1 + cos A

**∴ The correct answer is cos A + 1.**

questions.question: If the average of the squares of two consecutive odd natural numbers is 145, then the average of the two numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the average of the two consecutive odd numbers be A.

The numbers can be written as (A − 1) and (A + 1).

Average of their squares = [(A − 1)² + (A + 1)²] ÷ 2 = (2A² + 2) ÷ 2 = A² + 1

Given, A² + 1 = 145 ⇒ A² = 144 ⇒ A = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The average of the squares of two consecutive odd natural numbers is 145.

**Calculations:**

Let the two consecutive odd natural numbers be n and n + 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b13ae9bdbaebe99a30065559567c38d525978884377a95830d36857022537c34.png] 

⇒ Average of their squares = [n² + (n + 2)²] ÷ 2 = 145

⇒ n² + n² + 4n + 4 = 145 × 2

⇒ 2n² + 4n + 4 = 290

⇒ 2n² + 4n − 286 = 0

Dividing the equation by 2:

⇒ n² + 2n − 143 = 0

⇒ n² + 13n − 11n − 143 = 0

⇒ n(n + 13) − 11(n + 13) = 0

⇒ (n − 11)(n + 13) = 0

Since n is a natural number, n cannot be negative. Hence, n = 11.

The two numbers are 11 and (11 + 2) = 13.

Average of the numbers = (11 + 13) ÷ 2 = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Consecutive Odd Numbers

Consecutive odd numbers always have a difference of 2. They can be generally represented as 2k − 1 and 2k + 1, where k is a natural number.

Algebraic Identity for Squares

The sum of squares of (A − B) and (A + B) simplifies calculations directly: (A − B)² + (A + B)² = 2(A² + B²).

Average of Consecutive Numbers

The arithmetic mean or average of any two consecutive odd numbers is strictly the even number present exactly between them.

Find the **Range**: Maximum value (19) − Minimum value (11) = 8.

Find the **Mode**: The value with the highest frequency is 15 (appears 5 times).

Required **Mean** = (Range + Mode) ÷ 2

⇒ Mean = (8 + 15) ÷ 2 = 11.5.

**∴ The correct answer is 11.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Range = Maximum Observation − Minimum Observation

⇒ Range = 19 − 11 = 8

**Step 2: Calculate Mode**

⇒ Mode = Observation with maximum frequency

Mode is the value that appears **most frequently** in a data set. A set can be unimodal, bimodal, or multimodal.

Empirical Relationship

Arithmetic Mean

The mean of 'n' observations is the **sum** of all observations divided by the **total number** of observations.</p

questions.question: Half of the perimeter of a rectangle is 45 cm. If the length of a rectangle is 5 cm more than its breadth, then what is the area of ​​the rectangle?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Sum of dimensions (**L + B**) = 45 cm.

Difference between dimensions (**L − B**) = 5 cm.

**Length (L)** = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2 = (45 + 5) ÷ 2 = 25 cm.

**Breadth (B)** = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2 = (45 − 5) ÷ 2 = 20 cm.

**Area** = L × B = 25 × 20 = 500 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 500 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Half of the perimeter** = 45 cm | **Length (L)** = **Breadth (B)** + 5 cm.

Formula: **Area of rectangle** = Length × Breadth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c273374adcebc318342946d40b9d0ddaf0252a6bfc6cf12a153c1c1530b6bcbe.png] 

⇒ L + B = 45

⇒ (B + 5) + B = 45

⇒ 2B + 5 = 45

⇒ 2B = 40

⇒ **Breadth (B)** = 20 cm

⇒ **Length (L)** = 20 + 5 = 25 cm

⇒ **Area** = 25 × 20 = 500 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 500 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of Rectangle

The total distance around the rectangle is 2 × (Length + Breadth). Half perimeter is simply (Length + Breadth).

Diagonal of Rectangle

The diagonal (d) of a rectangle can be found using d = √(L² + B²).

Square Property

A square is a special rectangle where Length = Breadth, resulting in Area = Side².</p

questions.question: A sum triple itself in 9 years at simple interest. Find the rate of interest per annum is.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Rate (R) = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ T

Where n = number of times the sum becomes (n = 3) and T = Time (T = 9 years).

R = [(3 − 1) × 100] ÷ 9

R = 200 ÷ 9 = 22²/₉%

**∴ The correct answer is 22²/₉%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let Principal (P) = P

Amount (A) = 3P (Since the sum triples itself)

Time (T) = 9 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76acbb5040afb9734a91b27423d0afd9ccf9578245a14be2b58040dc667fe40f.png] 

⇒ SI = Amount − Principal

⇒ SI = 3P − P = 2P

⇒ 2P = (P × R × 9) ÷ 100

⇒ 2 = (R × 9) ÷ 100

⇒ 200 = 9R

⇒ R = 200 ÷ 9

⇒ R = 22²/₉%

**∴ The correct answer is 22²/₉%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Principle

In simple interest, the interest remains constant every year because it is always calculated on the original Principal (P).

Relationship between Time and Multiplier

If a sum becomes 'n' times in T years, then T = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ R. This allows for quick calculation of either Rate or Time.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

For the first year, SI and CI are equal if the interest is compounded annually. From the second year onwards, CI > SI because interest is earned on interest in CI.</p

questions.question: An inlet pipe fills up a cistern in 2 hours, while an outlet pipe empties it in 4 hours. The empty cistern was being filled up with both the pipes open for 1 hour, after which someone closed the outlet. How long will it take in total to fill up the cistern?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity = LCM of 2 and 4 = 4 units.

Efficiency: Inlet = +2 units/hr, Outlet = −1 unit/hr.

Volume filled in the 1st hour (both open) = 2 − 1 = +1 unit.

Remaining capacity to be filled = 4 − 1 = 3 units.

Total time = 1 hr (initial) + (3 ÷ 2) hr (remaining filled by inlet) = 2.5 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 hours 30 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

An inlet pipe fills the cistern in 2 hours.

An outlet pipe empties the cistern in 4 hours.

Both pipes are opened together for the first 1 hour.

**Calculations:**

Let Total Capacity be the LCM of given times (2 and 4).

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Hours**
 **Total Capacity**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Inlet Pipe
 2
 4
 4 ÷ 2 = 2
 
 

 Outlet Pipe
 4
 4 ÷ 4 = −1
 
 

⇒ Combined efficiency of both pipes when open = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hr.

⇒ Part of the cistern filled in the 1st hour = 1 × 1 = 1 unit.

⇒ Remaining capacity to be filled = 4 − 1 = 3 units.

⇒ After 1 hour, the outlet pipe is closed, meaning only the inlet pipe operates with an efficiency of 2 units/hr.

⇒ Time taken by the inlet pipe to fill the remaining cistern = 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5 hours.

⇒ 1.5 hours is equal to 1 hour 30 minutes.

⇒ Total time taken = 1 hour (initial time) + 1 hour 30 minutes (later time) = 2 hours 30 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 hours 30 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

An inlet pipe fills a tank, so its work is taken as positive. An outlet pipe (or leak) empties it, so its work is taken as negative.

Net Part Filled in 1 Hour

If an inlet pipe fills a tank in x hours and an outlet pipe empties it in y hours (where y > x), the net part filled in 1 hour is (1/x) − (1/y).

Time and Work Equivalence

Pipes and cisterns problems follow the exact same rules as standard Time & Work problems. Total capacity acts as total work, and the rate of filling/emptying acts as efficiency.

questions.question: What are the receptors for detecting taste called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Gustatory receptors**

• Receptors are the organs or cells which respond to light, heat or external stimulus and transmit the signal to the sensory nerve.
 
• Gustatory receptors are the receptors for detecting taste.
 
• **Sensory receptors** - These are broad categories of receptors responsible for converting external stimuli from the environment into internal electrical impulses that can be interpreted by the nervous system. Sensory receptors can be classified based on the type of stimulus they detect, such as mechanoreceptors for touch, thermoreceptors for temperature, and photoreceptors for light. 
 
• **Chemical receptors **- This term usually refers to receptors that detect chemical substances. It can encompass a wider range of receptor types, including those involved in taste (gustatory receptors), smell (olfactory receptors), and even some internal bodily functions (such as chemoreceptors that monitor carbon dioxide levels in the blood). 
 
• **Olfactory receptors **- These are specific to the** sense of smell**. Olfactory receptors are located in the olfactory epithelium, part of the nasal cavity, and are responsible for detecting odorous compounds in the air.
